findings.F1: The failing Calmar (0.499 against 0.75) comes from a book that sits in a position on 98 % of the coins' days and falls 43–45 % at its deepest; the 6049 bars with forecast below 2 hold only 0.037 of the book and earn about 0 (+0.0025 % a day), so the falls are made on signal days. Rebuilt at the same cost, keeping only forecast > 10 cuts the deepest fall to −37.6 % for a Calmar of 0.566, and halving every position gives a Calmar of 0.570 (fall −22.8 %, yearly +13 %); neither reaches 0.75.
findings.F2: The size of the move is the binding limit. The total move per case is +0.23 % against a 0.19 % cost per trade, 1.2 times the cost, and the unusual move of +0.11 % is 0.6 times the cost (strength 0.025). Only a stronger case of the situation can carry the fees.
findings.F3: Inside the signals (forecast > 10), the next-day excess return rises with the day's volume against its prior 20-day mean: by volume-ratio quartile (means 0.75, 1.07, 1.48, 2.99) it is +0.14 %, +0.06 %, +0.34 % and +0.56 %, with 1254 cases each. Keeping only signals with a ratio above 1.5 lifts the book to Sharpe 0.85 and Calmar 0.672, with its deepest fall cut to −24.7 %, the best of all the variants tried.
findings.F4: The effect lives on days that fell hard. On days down more than one prior 20-day standard deviation, signals earn +0.59 % excess next day (1622 cases), while the same down days without the signal earn −0.05 % (172 cases), so the down day alone is not the effect. Removing these down days from the book collapses it (Calmar 0.008, Sharpe 0.14). On days with |z| < 0.3, signals earn only +0.13 % (978 cases).
findings.F5: In the book's falls (days more than 15 % under its peak, 718 of 2898 days), signals earn −0.40 % excess next day (1516 cases), against +0.50 % outside them (4602 cases). The signal days inside the falls had a 20-day return of −7.6 % (against +4.9 % outside) and sat below their 50-day mean 80 % of the time (against 43 %). The falls come from signals taken inside the coin's own sustained declines.
findings.F6: The pooled slope of excess return on the forecast is t = 6.05 below the 50-day mean (12258 bars), against t = 0.55 above it (5122 bars). But below the 50-day mean the coin's drift is negative even without the signal (−0.25 % excess, 3296 bars), so restricting the book to below-the-mean bars loses money (Calmar −0.02). The trend state shifts the level of returns rather than repairing the book.
findings.F7: By the coin's 20-day volatility quartile, signals earn +0.66 % excess next day in the highest quartile (1614 cases), against −0.08 % to +0.03 % in the three others. The highest quartile without the signal earns −0.16 % (2011 cases), so high volatility alone is not the effect. Keeping only signals with volatility above its 120-day median cuts the deepest fall to −15.3 %, but the Calmar is 0.44 because the book trades much less.

ideas.idea: On a day whose volume is heavy against the coin's prior 20-day average, the lower the close sits within that day's high-low range, the more the coin rises over the next day, and this rise grows steeply with the volume ratio, so that the heaviest-volume days, well above their 20-day average, carry most of it.
ideas.consequence: A trader goes long for one day mainly after the heaviest-volume closes near the low, scaled by how far volume exceeds its 20-day average, and leaves ordinary heavy days alone because their move does not cover the fee.
ideas.name: Heaviest-volume low close rebounds

ideas.idea: On a day whose volume is heavy against the coin's prior 20-day average and whose return fell well below the coin's prior 20-day volatility, the lower the close sits within that day's high-low range, the more the coin rises over the next day, and the larger the day's fall against that volatility, the larger the rise.
ideas.consequence: A trader goes long for one day on a heavy-volume selloff that closed near its low, and does not treat a flat or rising heavy-volume day closing low as a reason to be long.
ideas.name: Heavy selloff low close rebound

ideas.idea: On a day whose volume is heavy against the coin's prior 20-day average, the lower the close sits within that day's high-low range, the more the coin rises over the next day, while the coin's 20-day volatility is high against its own past 120 days, and the higher that volatility, the larger the rise.
ideas.consequence: A trader takes the one-day long after a heavy-volume low close when the coin is in a volatile spell, and holds less or nothing on such days when the coin is calm.
ideas.name: Volatile-spell absorption rebound
